originalTitle: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
summary: The electoral commission said violence had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers".
content:
Counting began on Thursday evening as soon as polls had closed

Zambia's electoral commission has resumed the counting of votes from Thursday's presidential, parliamentary and local elections after it was halted over alleged attacks on polling staff.

The authority paused the process nationwide expressing concern about reports of violence that had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers in ballot boxes".

President Hakainde Hichilema is seeking a second five-year term. Brian Mundubile is the main opposition candidate among 13 challengers.

The electoral commission has set itself the target of announcing the results by the end of Sunday.

In its Friday evening update, the commission said that following a review of the situation and consultations with relevant law enforcement agencies "the security threat to the electoral process has been contained and the necessary measures have been put in place to enable the process to continue".

Counting initially got under way immediately after polls closed on Thursday but no official results had been declared when the halt came into effect.

Earlier on Friday, Mundubile expressed "grave concern" over delays in the announcement of presidential results, warning that the delay could create opportunities for interference or manipulation.

He cited what he described as "deeply troubling reports" from several areas, including alleged military involvement at tallying centres and allegations concerning the movement of ballot boxes.

He called for the immediate publication of results polling station by polling station, protection of the chain of custody and investigations into the reported incidents. He also said that his own party's tabulation of the results showed that he had won.

Hichilema also issued a statement urging Zambians to "remain peaceful, patient and patriotic as we await the official outcome from those entrusted with managing the vote".

Queues were seen at polling stations during a chilly Thursday morning in the capital, Lusaka

Polling day was largely peaceful, with queues reported in many areas and only isolated delays. Along with electing a president and MPs, the more than eight million registered voters had the chance to choose a new parliament and local councils.

Thursday's vote was seen as a test of Zambia's reputation as one of Africa's most stable democracies, amid concerns that political freedoms are being undermined.

Despite 14 candidates being on the presidential ballot paper, the contest was largely seen as a two-horse race between the incumbent and his main challenger Mundubile - running on the banner of the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP).

Hichilema is credited with steering Zambia through a difficult economic climate but his popularity was dented as many people said their circumstances have not improved. Mundubile hoped to capitalise on that dissatisfaction.

Mundubile is a former minister in the Patriotic Front (PF) government that ruled from 2011 to 2021, with his alliance drawing support from backers of the late former President, Edgar Lungu.

Officials marked voters' thumbnails with indelible ink to make sure they do not try to vote again

Lungu died more than a year ago and his body remains unburied in South Africa, amid a bitter dispute between Lungu's family and Hichilema, which has heightened political divisions in Zambia.

Hichilema, 64, won the 2021 election on his sixth attempt and is betting on job creation and an ambitious infrastructure drive to secure a second and final term.

The election was seen as a referendum on his economic record, which has boasted debt restructuring, currency strengthening and lowered inflation.

But his United Party for National Development (UPND) government has also been criticised by Amnesty International for restricting rights and freedoms , external in the run-up to this election, an accusation that Zambian authorities have yet to comment on.

A host of election officials were overseeing the process

Civil society monitors reported mostly orderly voting alongside some incidents of delays and procedural issues. International observers are present.

Mwiche Nalupumbwe, 26, was among hundreds who braved Thursday's morning chill to queue at polling stations well before they opened.

"Zambians are frustrated and this election is a 50-50, that is why we are all here early to make the change," he told the AFP news agency.

"I voted for HH because he cares about us," James Phiri, a 29-year-old student at the University of Zambia, told the Reuters news agency, using a common nickname for the president.

"Things are better after he re-introduced meal allowances," he said.

Samuel Chitendwe, a 47-year-old welder and father of four, said he voted for Mundubile.

"I have just come from firing someone. We are tired of stories about economic progress," he told Reuters.

If no presidential candidate gets more than 50% of the vote a run-off must be held within 37 days.

Additional reporting by Basillioh Rukanga Natasha Booty

Correction 14 August 2026: This story was amended to say the Sunday deadline for announcing the result was one set by the electoral commission and not the law.

chineseTitle: 赞比亚计票工作因涉嫌袭击投票站工作人员而暂停后恢复
chineseSummary: 选举委员会表示，暴力“导致标记选票被盗”。
chineseContent:
周四晚上投票结束后就开始计票

赞比亚选举委员会已恢复周四总统、议会和地方选举的计票工作，此前该委员会因涉嫌袭击投票站工作人员而暂停计票。

当局暂停了全国范围内的这一进程，对“导致投票箱中标记选票被盗”的暴力报道表示担忧。

总统哈凯恩德·希奇莱马正在寻求第二个五年任期。布赖恩·蒙杜比莱 (Brian Mundubile) 是 13 名挑战者中的主要反对派候选人。

选举委员会设定的目标是在周日结束前宣布结果。

该委员会在周五晚间发布的最新消息中表示，在对局势进行审查并与相关执法机构协商后，“选举进程的安全威胁已得到遏制，并已采取必要措施以使进程能够继续进行”。

计票工作最初在周四投票结束后立即开始，但在暂停生效时尚未宣布任何官方结果。

周五早些时候，蒙杜比勒对延迟公布总统选举结果表示“严重关切”，警告称延迟可能会创造干扰或操纵的机会。

他引用了来自多个领域的“令人深感不安的报告”，包括据称军事介入计票中心以及有关投票箱移动的指控。

他呼吁各投票站立即公布投票结果，保护监管链并对报告的事件进行调查。他还表示，他所在政党的结果列表显示他赢了。

希奇莱马还发表声明，敦促赞比亚人“在等待负责管理投票的人公布正式结果时保持和平、耐心和爱国”。

周四寒冷的早晨，首都卢萨卡的投票站前排起了长队。

投票日基本平静，据报道许多地区都出现排队现象，只有个别地区出现延误。除了选举总统和议员外，超过八百万登记选民还有机会选举新的议会和地方议会。

由于担心政治自由受到破坏，周四的投票被视为对赞比亚作为非洲最稳定民主国家之一声誉的考验。

尽管总统选票上有 14 名候选人，但这场竞争在很大程度上被视为现任总统和他的主要挑战者蒙杜比勒之间的两匹马竞赛——蒙杜比勒打着统一与繁荣民族和解党 (NRPUP) 的旗号。

希奇莱马因带领赞比亚度过了困难的经济气候而受到赞誉，但他的声望受到了削弱，因为许多人表示他们的情况没有改善。蒙杜比莱希望利用这种不满情绪。

蒙杜比莱是爱国阵线 (PF) 政府的前部长，该政府于 2011 年至 2021 年执政，他的联盟得到了已故前总统埃德加·伦古 (Edgar Lungu) 的支持者的支持。

官员用不可磨灭的墨水标记选民的缩略图，以确保他们不会再次尝试投票

伦古去世一年多前，他的尸体仍未埋葬在南非，伦古的家人与希奇莱马之间存在激烈争执，加剧了赞比亚的政治分歧。

64 岁的希奇莱马第六次赢得 2021 年大选，他押注于创造就业机会和雄心勃勃的基础设施建设，以确保连任第二个也是最后一个任期。

这次选举被视为对他的经济记录的公投，他的经济记录夸耀了债务重组、货币走强和降低通胀。

但他的国家发展联合党（UPND）政府也因在这次选举前夕限制外部权利和自由而受到国际特赦组织的批评，赞比亚当局尚未对这一指控发表评论。

许多选举官员正在监督整个过程

民间社会监督员报告称，投票大多有序，同时也出现一些延误和程序问题。国际观察员也在场。

26 岁的 Mwiche Nalupumbwe 是数百人中的一员，他们冒着星期四早晨的寒冷，在投票站开放前就到投票站排队。

他对法新社表示：“赞比亚人感到沮丧，这次选举的结果是 50 比 50，这就是为什么我们很早就来这里做出改变。”

“我投票给 HH，因为他关心我们，”赞比亚大学 29 岁的学生詹姆斯·菲里 (James Phiri) 告诉路透社，他使用了总统的常用昵称。

“在他重新推出膳食津贴后，情况好多了，”他说。

47 岁的焊工、四个孩子的父亲塞缪尔·奇滕维 (Samuel Chitendwe) 表示，他投票给了蒙杜比莱。

“我刚刚解雇了某人。我们厌倦了有关经济进步的故事，”他告诉路透社。

如果没有总统候选人获得超过 50% 的选票，则必须在 37 天内举行决选。

Basillioh Rukanga Natasha Booty 的补充报道

2026 年 8 月 14 日更正：本文经过修改，称宣布结果的周日截止日期是由选举委员会而非法律规定的。
